hints: Ask yourself why a trunk shrinks a little in the day. Think about water leaving leaves by transpiration faster than roots can replace it.
Now check the three circles: increased light intensity, increased wind speed and increased temperature. Which of these speed up transpiration and so would pull even more water out of the trunk?
walkthrough:
**Spot why the trunk shrinks**

Think of the trunk like a water-filled pipe. During the day, leaves lose water by transpiration.

If water loss from leaves is faster than water uptake by roots, cells in the stem lose turgor and the whole trunk shrinks slightly.

**Recall what increases transpiration**

Three main environmental factors increase the rate of transpiration. Increased light intensity opens stomata wider. Increased temperature increases evaporation and diffusion. Increased wind speed blows away humid air and maintains a steep diffusion gradient.

**Pick the region with all three**

To make the diameter decrease even more, you want maximum water loss. That means you need all three factors together.

In the Venn, D is the centre where light intensity, wind speed and temperature all overlap, so D is the answer.

options.A: A is only increased light intensity plus increased temperature. It misses wind speed, so transpiration would not be at its maximum.
options.B: B is only increased wind speed plus increased temperature. It misses light intensity, so stomata would not be as fully open.
options.C: C is only increased light intensity plus increased wind speed. It misses temperature, so evaporation would not be as fast.
options.D: D is the overlap of all three factors. Light, wind and temperature together give the highest transpiration rate and the greatest extra shrinkage.
